sources.title: UK Environmental Accounts: 2026
facts: ONS reports UK environmental-account greenhouse-gas emissions on a residence basis and explicitly distinguishes this accounting frame from territorial measures.
The 2024 residence-basis total and industry/household shares are national accounting statistics, not parcel measurements.

sources.title: UK Environmental Accounts: 2026 release page
facts: The ONS release page records the 5 June 2026 publication and links the associated environmental-account datasets.
Release metadata establishes publication/currentity context but does not itself create a parcel emissions observation.

sources.title: Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas
facts: ONS provides greenhouse-gas emissions by industry and gas for the UK from 1990 to 2024 with current and provisional editions.
These are residence-basis environmental-account data by industry, not emissions assigned to individual land parcels.

sources.title: Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas current edition
facts: The current ONS edition documents scheduled revisions and a March 2026 correction to some 2023 industry carbon-dioxide values in a prior file.
Revision history must be preserved; a superseded file must not silently override the current edition.

sources.title: Estimates of quarterly greenhouse gas emissions
facts: ONS quarterly greenhouse-gas estimates use a Chow-Lin regression-based temporal-disaggregation method.
Quarterly modeled estimates must remain distinct from annual inventory observations and from parcel measurements.

sources.title: Energy use by industry, source and fuel
facts: ONS publishes UK energy use by industry, source and fuel for 1990 to 2024.
Energy use is activity evidence and requires an explicit applicable emissions factor and scope before it can support an emissions calculation.

sources.title: Energy use by industry, source and fuel current edition
facts: The current ONS edition includes industry, source and fuel dimensions and retains revision history.
An industry energy-use row is not a parcel greenhouse-gas observation.

sources.title: Energy use: total current edition
facts: ONS reports direct and reallocated UK energy use by industry for 1990 to 2024.
National or industry energy totals cannot be assigned directly to an individual parcel.

sources.title: Energy use: fossil fuels by fuel type and industry
facts: ONS publishes fossil-fuel use by industry and fuel type, including natural gas and transport fuels, for 1990 to 2024.
Fuel-use quantities are activity data rather than direct greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: Energy use: fossil fuels by fuel type and industry current edition
facts: The current ONS edition records scheduled revisions and a March 2026 correction to incorrectly formatted 2023 fuel figures in a prior version.
Formatting or revision events must not be mistaken for physical changes in emissions.

sources.title: Energy use: fossil fuels by fuel type current edition
facts: ONS reports UK fossil-fuel use by fuel type from 1990 to 2024.
UK fuel totals are aggregate activity statistics, not parcel-level emissions measurements.

sources.title: Environmental taxes dataset
facts: ONS publishes UK environmental-tax revenue including energy, transport and pollution or resource taxes.
Tax revenue is monetary/accounting information and must not be substituted for physical emissions.

sources.title: Environmental taxes current edition
facts: The current ONS environmental-taxes edition documents revision history for the statistical series.
A tax value, tax share or revision is not a greenhouse-gas measurement.

sources.title: UK environmental taxes: 2025 cancelled standalone release
facts: ONS states the standalone UK environmental taxes 2025 release was cancelled and the dataset/commentary was instead included in UK Environmental Accounts 2026.
A cancelled release must not be treated as an independently observed publication or silently duplicated.

sources.title: NAEI Inventory methodology
facts: NAEI describes annual inventory preparation from data requests and verification through estimation, QA/QC, review, publication and archiving.
Inventory estimates can be recalculated across the historical time series when methods or data improve; version and method context must therefore be retained.

sources.title: NAEI National inventory system
facts: NAEI describes the UK Greenhouse Gas National Inventory System, including planning, preparation, QA/QC, compilation and key data-provider responsibilities.
National-inventory governance and data provenance do not create parcel-level measurements.

sources.title: NAEI Quality Assurance and Quality Control
facts: NAEI documents traceability, database units, revision/recalculation, uncertainty estimation and final change-review controls used for the inventory.
QA/QC evidence supports confidence and provenance but is not itself a physical emissions observation.

sources.title: NAEI About the inventory
facts: NAEI explains the integrated greenhouse-gas and air-quality inventory and its consistent use of activity and emission-factor data.
Inventory scope and governance must remain distinct from parcel binding.

sources.title: UK government conversion factors for company reporting collection
facts: DESNZ's collection states company-reporting conversion factors calculate Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions from activity data such as fuel, electricity or distance.
A conversion factor without supported activity data, scope and applicable period does not establish parcel emissions.

sources.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate statistics 2025 fifth provisional release
facts: DfT's fifth provisional 2025 SAF release is based on data available as of 8 July 2026 and remains incomplete until the final report planned for November 2026.
SAF volumes, SAFC balances and carbon/sustainability characteristics have aviation-fuel scope and are not land-parcel emissions.

sources.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate statistics data tables
facts: DfT's SAF data-table series records provisional fuel volumes, certificates, trades and carbon/sustainability characteristics.
Provisional table values can change before final publication and certificates are not physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate statistics collection
facts: DfT states provisional SAF figures are updated and revised before the final publication and describes the mandate's certificate-based framework.
Collection metadata and mandate obligations are not parcel emissions observations.

sources.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate statistics 2025 first provisional release
facts: The first provisional 2025 SAF release used data available as of 31 July 2025 and was explicitly incomplete.
Earlier provisional editions must not supersede later provisional or final data without version context.

sources.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate statistics 2025 second provisional release
facts: The second provisional 2025 SAF release used data available as of 27 October 2025 and remained incomplete.
Version ordering and provisional status must be preserved when comparing SAF statistics.

sources.title: UK ETS Hospital and Small Emitter status
facts: DESNZ states qualifying HSE installations have annual emissions targets, must monitor reportable emissions and submit annual emissions reports, while not surrendering allowances as main-scheme operators do.
An HSE target, eligibility threshold or carbon-price penalty formula is not the same as measured emissions from a land parcel.
